audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart (Skill/Rumble/Rumble/Skill/Skill/Rumble/Rumble) contradicts the packet chart and the content whys, which both describe an even level 1-2, Rumble owning 3 through 6, and Yone taking over from first item.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Skill, Skill, Rumble, Rumble, Rumble, Yone, Yone and every whys[] string matches that reading. A 57.17% win rate over 1436 games also supports Yone owning the item phases, not Rumble.
audit.corrected: Flip the chart in both layers to Skill, Skill, Rumble, Rumble, Rumble, Yone, Yone and realign the phase whys to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes are described without countable numbers on either side.
audit.why: Kit data gives The Equalizer 130/105/80s, Fate Sealed 120/100/80s, Soul Unbound 22/19/16/13/10s and Scrap Shield a flat 6s. Those turn 'wait for the cooldown' into a countable window.
audit.corrected: State The Equalizer's 130s rank-1 cooldown as the window Yone fights in, and Scrap Shield's 6s as the reason a single baited shield is not enough on its own.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Soul Unbound (E) an 'untargetable window'. Riot's description does not grant untargetability — the spirit leaves the body behind and Yone is forced back to that body, repeating a portion of the damage he dealt.
audit.why: Kit text for E: 'Yone's spirit leaves his body behind, gaining Move Speed. When this ability ends, Yone's spirit is forced back to his body and he repeats a portion of the damage he dealt as a spirit.' No untargetable flag is set. Asserting untargetability would tell a player to dive through The Equalizer expecting immunity.
audit.corrected: Describe Soul Unbound as a move-speed gap-close with a forced snap-back that repeats part of the spirit damage — and note the snap-back point is what Rumble aims The Equalizer at.

audit.why: Scrap Shield's 6s cooldown is short enough that baiting it alone does not open a full commit; the punishable cooldown is The Equalizer at 130s rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rumble's E and R carry the projectile flag; Yone has no projectile-blocking tool, so this is not actionable and should not be written.
audit.why: Relevance rule — no non-interactions on the page.

edits.before: W shield-grit covers every exchange you start. Only take the trade when Rumble's Scrap Shield is down.
edits.after: One ability and no banked heat yet, so level 2 stays even. Stack Mortal Steel to two before you step in.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Scrap Shield's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Flamespitter plus two stored Electro Harpoons hold you off the wave. Take the ranged minions and refuse the flamethrower cone entirely.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Rumble's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: The Equalizer is a 130-second carpet that owns the wave and any skirmish. Do not fight on it — spend Fate Sealed after it lands.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Scrap Shield's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — Q3 and Soul Unbound close through his slow the moment it finishes.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Rumble carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on and Rumble is a squishy 600-range mage: close with Soul Unbound, then Fate Sealed drags him in before he re-heats.

edits.before: Late, Rumble is a squishy short-range mage: your Soul Unbound (E) untargetable window plus R lets you dive onto him and kill him before he re-heats his kit.
edits.after: Late, Rumble is a squishy 600-range mage: Soul Unbound (E) repeats your spirit damage on the snap-back, so dive with it, dump the pattern, then Fate Sealed him.

edits.before: After your first item you flip it decisively — this is a 57% matchup for you late. Your Q3 dash and Soul Unbound (E) untargetable window let you close the gap through his slow, and once you're on top of a squishy, short-range Rumble your DPS plus R delete him before he re-heats. Look for picks whenever his Scrap Shield is down.
edits.after: After your first item you flip it decisively — this is a 57% matchup for you late. Your Q3 dash and Soul Unbound (E) speed boost close the gap through his slow, and once you're on top of a squishy 600-range Rumble your DPS plus Fate Sealed delete him before he re-heats. Fight on The Equalizer's 130-second cooldown, never on the carpet.

edits.before: At level 2 Rumble still lacks the tools to zone you, so it stays even.
edits.after: At level 2 Rumble still lacks the tools to zone you, so it stays even.

notes: The missingInteractions entry claims 'Both sides carry displacement (Mortal Steel (Q) vs Scrap Shield (W))' — that is a derived-flag misfire. Riot's Scrap Shield text is a shield plus a move-speed burst; there is no knockup and no terrain despite both flags being set. Do not write that interaction. Rumble's only displacement-adjacent tool is The Equalizer's terrain-like flame wall. Also: the full-layer tldr and winCon duplicate the same sentence ('build MR and bait his shield' twice in tldr) — left alone here because a rewrite would need a length-band-safe rebuild, but it reads badly on the live page. Level-chart rows were proposed as matched full/content pairs across the whole chart as one group. phases[2] side is unchanged (Rumble) and included only to keep the chart group atomic.
